statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Tail sits in the low band well below the block threshold, while Stress is elevated on the oil-led inflation impulse and hawkish Fed repricing.
recommendation: Conditions are consistent with a contained, two-sided regime in which mean reversion is still functioning. The narrow evidence-based danger window covers the S&P Global Manufacturing PMI, ISM Manufacturing PMI and JOLTS releases on 1 September between 13:45 and 15:00 UTC, where conditional Tail peaks in the watch band. Existing-position management and emergency protection remain unaffected by this descriptive assessment.
headline: Nasdaq-100 holds a two-sided range as Gulf escalation lifts crude and hawkish Fed repricing raises Stress
body: The Nasdaq-100 is trading near 29,355, about 0.27 percent lower, inside a narrow 29,304 to 29,465 session range, with the index sitting mid-range rather than pinned to an extreme. VIX is 15.15, up roughly 5 percent but still low in absolute terms. The broader tape is weaker than the Nasdaq: the S&P 500 is down about 0.5 percent and the Russell 2000 about 0.9 percent, so breadth is soft while megacap and semiconductor pricing is comparatively resilient. Two macro channels dominate. First, renewed Strait of Hormuz escalation has pushed WTI up about 2.7 percent to roughly 85.6 dollars and Brent above 90 dollars after US strikes on Iranian rocket launchers on Larak Island and Iranian strikes on US facilities in Jordan. Second, Federal Reserve Chairman Warsh's 28 August Jackson Hole remarks flagged inflation as still too high with PCE at 3.7 percent, leaving September rate-hike expectations close to a coin flip and long-end Treasury yields elevated, with the 10-year near 4.75 percent. Both channels widen the distribution of outcomes, which is why Stress is elevated. Neither has yet produced the price-path signature that matters for Tail: there is no persistent one-way structure, retracements are occurring, pullbacks are not unusually shallow, and the index is not holding session extremes. Tail therefore stays low. The identified checkpoints are the August month-end cash close later today and the simultaneous ISM Manufacturing and JOLTS releases at 14:00 UTC on 1 September, which carry the clearest mechanism for a repricing leg that could deny retracement.

lookbackSummary: The past 24 hours began with a quiet, low-risk late Monday-into-Tuesday profile, with Tail near 5 and Stress in the high twenties. Risk stepped up overnight as the Gulf escalation and crude move were priced in, with Tail peaking at 15 and a brief trend-down read around 00:00 UTC, then decaying through the Asian and European sessions back to single digits by 07:00-08:00 UTC. A second, larger step came with the European and US repricing of the hawkish Jackson Hole message and the oil spike, lifting Stress from the high thirties into the low fifties from 09:00 UTC onward while Tail stayed in the low teens. Every hour of the window carried a published assessment, and the action remained EA_ON throughout.
outlookSummary: The next 24 hours contain two identifiable checkpoints. The nearer one is the August month-end cash close at 20:00 UTC, where rebalancing and closing imbalances typically widen swings; that is treated as a Stress event rather than a Tail event, since whipsaw generally preserves mean reversion. Conditional risk then decays through the thin Globex reopen and the Asian and European sessions, with Gulf headline risk the residual overnight asymmetry. The path rises again into the US session on 1 September and peaks in the watch band at 14:00 UTC, when the ISM Manufacturing PMI and JOLTS Job Openings release simultaneously as the first hard data since the hawkish Jackson Hole shift and with September hike odds near a coin flip. That combination is the clearest mechanism for a repricing leg capable of denying retracement, so the danger window is drawn narrowly around 13:45 to 15:00 UTC. All forecast values are conditional; no future price-path structure is treated as already observed.

A persistent late drift would be the conditional escalation checkpoint.

forecast.analysis: US cash close and month-end print. Liquidity thins as index futures carry the session forward alone, and residual imbalance unwind can produce sharp but usually reverting moves. Conditional risk eases once the close is absorbed and futures settle into a defined post-close range.

forecast.analysis: Post-close hour. With month-end flow completed, conditional Tail normally decays as volatility drains and futures settle. Gulf headline risk remains the residual asymmetry, since a fresh escalation report is the main plausible source of a gapped repricing at this hour.
